rows.why: S1 covers the basic result shape: feature name, scenarios in file order, and each step's keyword as written, its text and its line. No item asks about this. Item 12 asks whether text like 'Andrew' counts as a step keyword, which is a different behaviour from what S1 fixes.

Item 4 asks how tags are handled and which scenario gets them. The pick splits @ lines on whitespace and attaches them to the next Scenario, which is what S2 expects. Item 7's pick about header description lines touches another part of S2, but item 4 is the closest.

Item 5 asks whether a Background is supported and how it is returned. The pick returns the background steps in a separate field, which matches S3's 'returned as the background, not copied into the scenarios'.

Item 8 asks how doc strings and tables are returned. The pick attaches them to the preceding step, strips the opening indent from doc string lines and trims table cells, all as S4 expects. Also accepting ``` goes beyond S4 but does not contradict it.

S5 bundles several error cases, and items 2, 6, 7, 9 and 10 each cover one. All of their picks agree with S5. Item 9 is the closest because it asks directly at which line an error is reported, and its pick (the opening line) matches. Item 1 is not a match: it asks about a file with no Feature line at all (empty or only comments), while S5 is about content that comes before the Feature line.

No item asks whether a feature with no scenarios is valid. Item 12 is about a scenario with no steps, item 1 about a file with no Feature line, and item 5 only implies that a missing Background returns null.
